```{python}
#| tags: [parameters]

FILE = "scdownstream_annotate.h5ad"
# Comma-separated prediction columns added by this run, e.g. celltypist:<model>,scanvi:<model>
PREDICTION_COLS = ""
# Description of the cell subset, e.g. "leiden: 3, 7"; empty for all cells
SUBSET = ""
UMAP_FOR_PLOTS = "X_umap_scvi"
MAX_CELLTYPE_LABELS = 50
VERSIONS_FILE = "versions.yml"
# Cells with a lower confidence are counted as low-confidence predictions
LOW_CONFIDENCE = 0.5
# Labels per axis of the agreement heatmaps; the others are grouped as "other"
MAX_HEATMAP_LABELS = 30
```

```{python}
max_predicted_labels = int(MAX_CELLTYPE_LABELS)
low_confidence = float(LOW_CONFIDENCE)
max_heatmap_labels = int(MAX_HEATMAP_LABELS)
subset_description = str(SUBSET).strip() if SUBSET and str(SUBSET).strip().lower() not in ("none", "null") else ""

# obs column prefixes of the label prediction tools; the confidence of <col> is in <col>:conf
prediction_prefixes = ('celltypist:', 'scanvi:')
method_titles = {'celltypist': 'CellTypist', 'scanvi': 'scANVI'}


def parse_list_param(value):
    # comma-separated -P value; quarto passes an empty value as null
    if value is None:
        return []
    items = [item.strip() for item in str(value).split(",")]
    return list(dict.fromkeys(item for item in items if item and item.lower() not in ("none", "null")))


def resolve_umap(adata, requested):
    requested = str(requested).strip() if requested else ""
    for key in ([requested, f"X_{requested}"] if requested else []):
        if key in adata.obsm:
            return key, None
    for key in ["X_umap_scvi", "X_umap_pca", "X_umap"]:
        if key in adata.obsm:
            note = (f"UMAP '{requested}' was not found in adata.obsm, plotting '{key}' instead. "
                    f"Available: {', '.join(adata.obsm.keys())}.") if requested else None
            return key, note
    raise ValueError(f"No UMAP found in adata.obsm (available: {', '.join(adata.obsm.keys())})")


def group_predicted_labels(values, max_labels):
    # cells per label, most cells first; the labels after the first max_labels are grouped as "other"
    counts = values.value_counts()
    counts = counts[counts > 0]
    top, rest = counts.iloc[:max_labels], counts.iloc[max_labels:]
    return top, rest, f"other ({len(rest)} labels)"


def grouped_labels_note(top, rest):
    return (f"Showing the {len(top)} labels with the most cells out of {len(top) + len(rest)}; "
            f"the other {len(rest)} labels ({rest.sum()} cells)")


def grouped_values(values, top, rest, other_name):
    # labels outside the top labels replaced by other_name
    return values if rest.empty else values.where(values.isin(top.index), other_name)


def label_colors(labels, other_name):
    # scanpy's default colours for this many categories (default_102), grey for "other"
    palette = sc.pl.palettes.default_102
    return [("lightgrey" if label == other_name else palette[i % len(palette)]) for i, label in enumerate(labels)]


def method_of(col):
    method, _, model = col.partition(':')
    return method_titles.get(method, method), model


def inline_table_html(df, index=False):
    """
    A table on a single line, for printing from an `output: asis` cell: pandoc reads the
    indentation of to_html's rows as an indented code block, so every line is stripped.
    """
    return ''.join(line.strip() for line in df.to_html(index=index, na_rep='').splitlines())


def scroll_table_html(df, index=False, max_height=400):
    return (f"<div style='overflow-y: scroll; overflow-x: auto; max-height: {max_height}px'>"
            f"{inline_table_html(df, index=index)}</div>")


def details_html(summary, body):
    return f"<details><summary><font color='green'>{summary}</font> - click to expand table</summary>{body}</details>"


def figure_html(fig, alt, caption=None):
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buffer, format='png', dpi=100, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close(fig)
    image = base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode('utf-8')
    caption_html = f"<figcaption>{escape_html(caption)}</figcaption>" if caption else ""
    return f'<figure><img alt="{escape_html(alt)}" src="data:image/png;base64,{image}" />{caption_html}</figure>'


def note_html(text):
    return f"<p><b>Note:</b> {text}</p>"
```

```{python}
adata = sc.read(FILE, backed="r")
obs = adata.obs.copy()
n_cells, n_genes = adata.n_obs, adata.n_vars

# UMAP for the plots, set by --umap_for_plots; external objects may have none
umap_notes = []
try:
    umap_key, umap_note = resolve_umap(adata, UMAP_FOR_PLOTS)
    if umap_note:
        umap_notes.append(umap_note)
    umap_coords = np.asarray(adata.obsm[umap_key])[:, :2]
except ValueError as err:
    umap_key, umap_coords = None, None
    umap_notes.append(f"{err}; the UMAP plots are skipped.")

adata.file.close()

# Prediction columns of this run: label columns, with their confidence in <col>:conf
requested_cols = parse_list_param(PREDICTION_COLS)
column_notes = []
if not requested_cols:
    requested_cols = [col for col in obs.columns if col.startswith(prediction_prefixes) and not col.endswith(':conf')]
    column_notes.append("No prediction columns given; showing all prediction columns of the object.")
label_cols = list(dict.fromkeys(col[:-len(':conf')] if col.endswith(':conf') else col for col in requested_cols))
missing_cols = [col for col in label_cols if col not in obs.columns]
label_cols = [col for col in label_cols if col in obs.columns]
if missing_cols:
    column_notes.append(f"Prediction column(s) not found in the object: {escape_html(', '.join(missing_cols))}.")


def conf_col_of(col):
    conf = f"{col}:conf"
    return conf if conf in obs.columns else None


def labels_of(col):
    values = obs[col]
    return values.astype(object).where(values.notna(), 'missing').astype(str)


def confidence_of(col):
    conf = conf_col_of(col)
    return pd.to_numeric(obs[conf], errors='coerce') if conf else None


group_col = 'sample' if 'sample' in obs.columns else 'batch' if 'batch' in obs.columns else None
```

```{python}
#| output: asis

subset_html = ""
if subset_description:
    subset_html = (f" The stage annotated only the cells selected by <b>{escape_html(subset_description)}</b> "
                   # &#45;&#45;: pandoc's smart typography would turn a printed "--" into an en dash
                   "(<code>&#45;&#45;annotate_subset_col</code> / <code>&#45;&#45;annotate_subset_values</code>), and the "
                   "annotated object holds only these cells.")
print(f"\n<p>The annotated object holds {n_cells} cells and {n_genes} genes.{subset_html}</p>\n")

counts = []
if 'sample' in obs.columns:
    counts.append(f"{obs['sample'].nunique()} samples")
if 'batch' in obs.columns:
    counts.append(f"{obs['batch'].nunique()} batches")
if counts:
    print(f"\n<p>{' and '.join(counts)}.</p>\n")

for note in column_notes + umap_notes:
    print(f"\n{note_html(note)}\n")

if not label_cols:
    print("\n<p>No prediction columns to report.</p>\n")
else:
    rows = []
    for col in label_cols:
        method, model = method_of(col)
        values = labels_of(col)
        conf = confidence_of(col)
        rows.append({
            'column': col,
            'method': method,
            'model': model,
            'labels predicted': int(values.nunique()),
            'median confidence': '' if conf is None else f"{conf.median():.3f}",
            f'% cells below {low_confidence:g} confidence': '' if conf is None else f"{100 * (conf < low_confidence).mean():.1f}",
        })
    print("\n<p>Prediction columns added by this run:</p>\n")
    print(f"\n{inline_table_html(pd.DataFrame(rows))}\n")
```

## <font color='green'>Predictions</font>

CellTypist (columns `celltypist:<model>`) predicts with pre-trained logistic regression models; its confidence (`:conf`) is the probability of the predicted label. scANVI (columns `scanvi:<model>`) maps the cells onto a pre-trained reference model (scArches), and its confidence is the probability of the most likely label. The latent space of the scANVI mapping is stored in `obsm['X_scanvi_<model>']`.

```{python}
#| output: asis

def umap_panels_html(col, values, top, rest, other_name, conf):
    grouped = grouped_values(values, top, rest, other_name).to_numpy()
    categories = [*top.index] + ([] if rest.empty else [other_name])
    # "other" cells first, so they are drawn below the coloured cells
    order = np.argsort(grouped != other_name, kind='stable')
    plot_obs = pd.DataFrame({'label': pd.Categorical(grouped[order], categories=categories)},
                            index=obs.index[order].astype(str))
    panels = [('label', col)]
    if conf is not None:
        plot_obs['confidence'] = conf.to_numpy()[order]
        panels.append(('confidence', f"{col}:conf"))
    adata_plot = ad.AnnData(obs=plot_obs, obsm={umap_key: umap_coords[order]})

    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, len(panels), figsize=(len(panels) * 8, 6), squeeze=False, layout='constrained')
    for ax, (panel, title) in zip(axs.ravel(), panels):
        if panel == 'label':
            sc.pl.embedding(adata_plot, basis=umap_key, color=panel, ax=ax, show=False, title=title,
                            palette=label_colors(categories, other_name), legend_fontsize=7)
        else:
            sc.pl.embedding(adata_plot, basis=umap_key, color=panel, ax=ax, show=False, title=title,
                            vmin=0, vmax=1)
    return figure_html(fig, f"{col} on the UMAP")


for col in label_cols:
    method, model = method_of(col)
    print(f"\n### <font color='green'>{escape_html(method)}: {escape_html(model)}</font>\n")

    values = labels_of(col)
    conf = confidence_of(col)
    top, rest, other_name = group_predicted_labels(values, max_predicted_labels)

    # top labels, then one row with the cells of all other labels
    count_table = pd.DataFrame({'label': top.index, 'cells': top.to_numpy()})
    if not rest.empty:
        count_table = pd.concat([count_table, pd.DataFrame({'label': [other_name], 'cells': [rest.sum()]})],
                                ignore_index=True)
    count_table['% cells'] = (100 * count_table['cells'] / len(values)).round(1)
    table_note = "" if rest.empty else note_html(f"{grouped_labels_note(top, rest)} are summed in the last row.")
    print(f"\n{details_html(f'Cells per label ({len(top) + len(rest)} labels)', table_note + scroll_table_html(count_table))}\n")

    if conf is None:
        print(f"\n{note_html(f'No confidence column {escape_html(col)}:conf.')}\n")
    else:
        n_low = int((conf < low_confidence).sum())
        print(f"\n<p>{n_low} of {len(conf)} cells ({100 * n_low / len(conf):.1f}%) have a confidence below "
              f"{low_confidence:g}.</p>\n")
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.5))
        ax.hist(conf.dropna().to_numpy(), bins=50, range=(0, 1), color='tab:blue')
        ax.axvline(low_confidence, color='grey', linestyle='--')
        ax.set_xlabel('confidence')
        ax.set_ylabel('cells')
        ax.set_title(f"{col}:conf")
        print(f"\n{figure_html(fig, f'{col} confidence histogram')}\n")

    if umap_key is not None:
        print(f"\n{umap_panels_html(col, values, top, rest, other_name, conf)}\n")
        if not rest.empty:
            print(f"\n{note_html(grouped_labels_note(top, rest) + ' are shown in grey as other.')}\n")
```

## <font color='green'>Agreement between the methods</font>

```{python}
#| output: asis

def crosstab_html(col_a, col_b):
    values_a, values_b = labels_of(col_a), labels_of(col_b)
    top_a, rest_a, other_a = group_predicted_labels(values_a, max_heatmap_labels)
    top_b, rest_b, other_b = group_predicted_labels(values_b, max_heatmap_labels)
    table = pd.crosstab(grouped_values(values_a, top_a, rest_a, other_a),
                        grouped_values(values_b, top_b, rest_b, other_b))
    rows = [label for label in [*top_a.index, other_a] if label in table.index]
    columns = [label for label in [*top_b.index, other_b] if label in table.columns]
    # fraction of the cells of each row label (col_a) predicted as each column label (col_b)
    fractions = table.loc[rows, columns]
    fractions = fractions.div(fractions.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan), axis=0).fillna(0)

    n_rows, n_cols = fractions.shape
    font_size = 8 if max(n_rows, n_cols) <= 30 else 6
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(min(max(5, 0.3 * n_cols + 3), 22), min(max(4, 0.3 * n_rows + 2), 22)))
    image = ax.imshow(fractions.to_numpy(), cmap='Blues', vmin=0, vmax=1, aspect='auto')
    ax.set_xticks(range(n_cols))
    ax.set_xticklabels(fractions.columns, rotation=90, fontsize=font_size)
    ax.set_yticks(range(n_rows))
    ax.set_yticklabels(fractions.index, fontsize=font_size)
    ax.set_xlabel(col_b)
    ax.set_ylabel(col_a)
    fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, fraction=0.03, pad=0.02, label=f'fraction of the {col_a} label')
    fig.tight_layout()

    caption = (f"Rows: the labels of {col_a}, each summing to 1; columns: the labels of {col_b} of the same cells.")
    if not (rest_a.empty and rest_b.empty):
        caption += f" At most {max_heatmap_labels} labels per axis are shown; the others are grouped as 'other'."
    return figure_html(fig, f"{col_a} vs {col_b}", caption)


if len(label_cols) < 2:
    print("\n<p>Only one prediction column; there is nothing to compare.</p>\n")
else:
    rows = []
    for col_a, col_b in itertools.combinations(label_cols, 2):
        same = labels_of(col_a) == labels_of(col_b)
        rows.append({'column 1': col_a, 'column 2': col_b,
                     'cells with the same label': int(same.sum()), '% cells': f"{100 * same.mean():.1f}"})
    print("\n<p>The labels are compared as text, so models with different label names (e.g. trained on "
          "different references) agree only where their names match; the heatmaps show how the labels "
          "of one column are split across the labels of the other.</p>\n")
    print(f"\n{inline_table_html(pd.DataFrame(rows))}\n")
    for col_a, col_b in itertools.combinations(label_cols, 2):
        print(f"\n{crosstab_html(col_a, col_b)}\n")
```

## <font color='green'>Clusters</font>

```{python}
#| output: asis

clustering_col = 'leiden'


def cluster_order(clusters):
    # numerical order for numbered clusters, text order otherwise
    names = list(clusters.unique())
    return sorted(names, key=int) if all(name.isdigit() for name in names) else sorted(names)


if clustering_col not in obs.columns:
    print(f"\n<p>No <code>{clustering_col}</code> column in the object; the per-cluster summary is skipped.</p>\n")
elif not label_cols:
    print("\n<p>No prediction columns.</p>\n")
else:
    clusters = obs[clustering_col].astype(str)
    order = cluster_order(clusters)
    summary = pd.DataFrame({'cluster': order, 'cells': clusters.value_counts().reindex(order).to_numpy()})
    for col in label_cols:
        table = pd.crosstab(clusters, labels_of(col)).reindex(order)
        summary[f'{col}: majority label'] = table.idxmax(axis=1).to_numpy()
        summary[f'{col}: fraction'] = (table.max(axis=1) / table.sum(axis=1)).map(lambda v: f"{v:.2f}").to_numpy()
    print(f"\n<p>The most frequent label of each method in each <code>{clustering_col}</code> cluster, and the "
          "fraction of the cluster's cells with that label.</p>\n")
    print(f"\n{scroll_table_html(summary)}\n")
```

## <font color='green'>Label composition per sample</font>

```{python}
#| output: asis

def composition_plot_html(col, fractions, colors):
    n_groups, n_labels = fractions.shape
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, min(max(3, 0.3 * n_groups + 1.5), 30)))
    left = np.zeros(n_groups)
    for label, color in zip(fractions.columns, colors):
        widths = fractions[label].to_numpy()
        ax.barh(np.arange(n_groups), widths, left=left, color=color, label=label)
        left += widths
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n_groups))
    ax.set_yticklabels(fractions.index, fontsize=8)
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
    ax.set_xlabel('fraction of cells')
    ax.set_title(col)
    ax.legend(loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1), fontsize=7, frameon=False,
              ncol=1 if n_labels <= 25 else 2)
    return figure_html(fig, f"{col} per {group_col}")


if group_col is None:
    print("\n<p>The object has no <code>sample</code> or <code>batch</code> column; the composition per sample "
          "is skipped.</p>\n")
elif not label_cols:
    print("\n<p>No prediction columns.</p>\n")
else:
    groups = obs[group_col].astype(str)
    print(f"\n<p>Share of each label among the cells of each {group_col} (column <code>{group_col}</code>).</p>\n")
    for col in label_cols:
        method, model = method_of(col)
        print(f"\n### <font color='green'>{escape_html(method)}: {escape_html(model)}</font>\n")
        values = labels_of(col)
        top, rest, other_name = group_predicted_labels(values, max_predicted_labels)
        columns = [*top.index] + ([] if rest.empty else [other_name])
        table = pd.crosstab(groups, grouped_values(values, top, rest, other_name)).reindex(columns=columns, fill_value=0)
        table = table.loc[sorted(table.index)]
        fractions = table.div(table.sum(axis=1), axis=0)

        percent_table = (100 * fractions).round(1)
        percent_table.insert(0, 'cells', table.sum(axis=1), allow_duplicates=True)
        percent_table.columns.name = None
        percent_table.index.name = group_col
        table_note = "" if rest.empty else note_html(f"{grouped_labels_note(top, rest)} are summed as other.")
        print(f"\n{details_html(f'% cells per label and {group_col}', table_note + scroll_table_html(percent_table.reset_index()))}\n")
        print(f"\n{composition_plot_html(col, fractions, label_colors(columns, other_name))}\n")
```

## <font color='green'>Software versions</font>

The first table lists the software of the pipeline modules that produced the results in
this report, as collected by Nextflow. The second one is read from the rendering
environment itself, so it describes the software that produced the report.

```{python}
def pipeline_versions(path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Software versions collected by Nextflow from the modules of this stage.

    The file is the collated versions.yml of the pipeline: one mapping per process, each
    holding the tools that process reported. It is flattened into one row per tool so the
    table reads the same way as the one below.
    """
    import yaml

    collected = {}
    if os.path.exists(path):
        with open(path) as handle:
            collected = yaml.safe_load(handle) or {}

    rows = [
        (process, tool, str(version))
        for process, tools in collected.items()
        for tool, version in (tools or {}).items()
    ]

    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['process', 'software', 'version'])


modules = pipeline_versions(str(VERSIONS_FILE))

display(HTML('<font color="black">' + modules.to_html(index=False) + '</font>'))
```

```{python}
import platform
import shutil
import subprocess

import IPython


def library_version(module) -> str:
    """
    Version of an already imported library.

    The attribute is preferred over the installed distribution metadata because it is what
    the running code reports about itself; the metadata is only consulted as a fallback.
    """
    reported = getattr(module, '__version__', None)
    if reported:
        return str(reported)

    from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version as distribution_version

    try:
        return distribution_version(module.__name__)
    except PackageNotFoundError:
        return 'unknown'


def quarto_version():
    """
    Version of the quarto binary rendering this document, or None if it cannot be read.

    Quarto does not export its own version into the rendering environment, so the binary is
    asked directly. The row is dropped rather than guessed when no binary can be reached.
    """
    reported = os.environ.get('QUARTO_VERSION')
    if reported and reported.strip():
        return reported.strip()

    bin_path = os.environ.get('QUARTO_BIN_PATH')
    candidates = [os.path.join(bin_path, 'quarto')] if bin_path else []
    candidates.append(shutil.which('quarto'))

    for candidate in candidates:
        if not candidate or not os.path.exists(candidate):
            continue
        try:
            completed = subprocess.run(
                [candidate, '--version'],
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=60,
                check=True,
            )
        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
            continue
        if completed.stdout.strip():
            return completed.stdout.strip()

    return None
```
